Pending local secrets were deleted after the matching request was acknowledged. This does not prove server-side credential revocation; use the PC to revoke an approved request.

The credential may be unknown or revoked on Runner. It is retained locally unless deletion was already confirmed. Check authentication explicitly or use local deletion; lost-device revocation belongs on the PC.
The local credential and reference were deleted. Runner-side revocation is not confirmed.
The Runner action could not be completed. Check the exact endpoint, certificate, network, and local-network permission, then retry explicitly. No HTTP fallback is used.
Endpoint changes are never inferred from DNS or redirects. Create a new invitation for the exact new endpoint and paste its payload below.

This creates a new principal after PC approval. A validated request for the same Runner replaces its local credential; rejection will require another invitation. Previous server credentials are not revoked, and resource ownership is not transferred. Revoke old credentials on the PC if needed.

The exact HTTPS endpoint will be replaced through a new manual pairing, with certificate validation and PC approval. This creates a new principal; old server credentials are not revoked and old resource ownership is not inherited. Continue?
Compare the fingerprint on the PC, then explicitly approve this request there. This screen polls only the restricted pairing status endpoint.
Paste the one-line Base64url payload printed by the Runner CLI. It contains a short-lived secret and is not persisted in saved UI state.
Nothing is sent until a complete payload validates locally.
Valid fields: HTTPS endpoint, Runner ID, root pin, invitation, and expiry.
Invalid, expired, non-canonical, or oversized payload.

A lost device must be revoked from the Runner PC. Local deletion alone does not revoke the server credential.
Runner-side revocation is requested first. The local credential is deleted only after a durable confirmation; a lost response is shown as unknown, not success.

The store is intentionally bounded and rotates at 4 MiB, so older records may be missing. If the selected provider fails after opening the destination, an incomplete file may remain; ReproDroid will not show it as saved.
Review the file before sharing. Operational messages are structured and secret-safe, but this export is not an anonymized diagnostic package.
